ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that in the right $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC=6$, $BC=4$. Rotating $\triangle ABC$ clockwise by $90^\circ$ around the right angle vertex $C$ yields $\triangle DEC$. If the point $F$ is the midpoint of $DE$, and $AF$ is connected, what is the length of $AF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let FG$\perp$AC, \\
according to the properties of rotation, EC=BC=4, DC=AC=6, $\angle$ACD=$\angle$ACB=$90^\circ$, \\
since point F is the midpoint of DE, \\
therefore FG$\parallel$CD \\
therefore $\triangle EFG\sim \triangle EDC$ \\
therefore $\frac{GF}{CD}=\frac{EF}{ED}=\frac{EG}{EC}=\frac{1}{2}$ \\
therefore GF=$\frac{1}{2}$CD=$\frac{1}{2}$AC=3 \\
EG=$\frac{1}{2}$EC=$\frac{1}{2}$BC=2 \\
since AC=6, EC=BC=4 \\
therefore AE=2 \\
therefore AG=4 \\
According to the Pythagorean theorem, $AF=\sqrt{AG^{2}+GF^{2}}=\sqrt{4^{2}+3^{2}}=\boxed{5}$

therefore AG=4 \\
